#4529. Mercedes Wants To Rethink EV Batteries With This Clever New Technology

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Mercedes-Benz wants to flip the script on how electric car high-voltage batteries work. Its new Power Converter, which is still in the development stage, can control the charge and discharge of individual cells inside the battery, which is a big change from how the vast majority of EV batteries work today.

For decades, traction batteries have had thousands of individual cells, which are arranged into cell groups or modules. The car’s brain can monitor the voltage of each cell or module, but when it comes to charging or discharging, everything gets the same treatment. Does the electric motor require 100 kilowatts? The whole pack delivers 100 kW. Charging at 150 kW? All the cells get treated equally.

With Mercedes’ new technology, however, each cell inside the pack can not only be monitored, but also controlled by a programmable micro-converter. In theory, the approach has a lot of advantages, including prolonging a car’s battery life, using different cell chemistries inside the same pack, and removing bulky power electronics that handle AC and DC conversion.

Let’s look at the longevity aspect first. When an EV battery fails, it’s usually because one or more cells inside the pack can no longer sustain the same voltage as their neighbors. The car throws a scary error message on the screen, and the dealer or service center will recommend replacing the entire battery, which costs a lot of money if the warranty has run out.

With Mercedes-Benz’s new approach, if a cell can no longer sustain the required voltage, it can be simply disabled by its micro-converter. Sure, the battery capacity goes down a smidge, but the car will still work as before.

By using multiple converters in parallel, the system can regulate the energy flow of individual cells or cell groups, removing the need for a single big converter. What’s more, if cells of varying chemistries or ages are bundled in the same pack, the micro-converters can make sure that they all get charged properly, albeit at different power levels. The same goes for the high-voltage output, which will no longer be tied to the number of cells connected in series, but to the converters and their software-based control.

The technology also enables a more modular approach to battery use. For instance, if a large-capacity battery isn’t used at full potential most of the time—say the owner drives only 50 miles daily—the car’s brain can put part of the pack in standby mode, keeping the cells at the right level for preservation. Then, when a long-distance road trip is being planned, the computer can unlock the full capacity.

Bidirectional charging is baked into the Power Converter. This means that AC and DC conversion, as well as bidirectional charging, are handled directly by the micro-converters, enabling finer control over how the battery is used.

Mercedes-Benz said that the new technology has the potential to boost the driving range and efficiency of future plug-in models, though there is one big asterisk that the company conveniently left out. With thousands of micro-converters sealed inside a battery pack, it inevitably means that there are thousands of components that can fail. If done right, though, it can bring a new level of modularity and fine-tuning to EV batteries.

#4528. How to Choose the Best Car Battery

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

Here's what you need to know to choose the right battery for your vehicle.

We've all experienced the stomach-churning trauma of a dead car battery. You need to be somewhere and you're running late. You jump in, twist the key or push the start button, and . . . nothing! Or maybe just a sickening click-click. Suddenly you need a jump-start or, worse, a tow. And probably a new battery, too. But which one?

So many brands, types, prices, and places to buy them. Which to choose and why? You don't need to be an expert to make an informed, cost-efficient purchase. Here are some brands we trust, but always check your owner’s manual for details and recommendations.

Check your owner's manual for your original battery's size, specifications, and ratings. You can also find which one you need from guides in the auto-parts store or online.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011

Replacing a battery yourself is an option; it's not particularly difficult. Some shops offer free installation—but only if the battery is purchased from them.

If you're buying one of the batteries above online and installing it yourself, be sure to check your owner's manual for critical information before purchasing your new battery. Modern cars have specific requirements on their electrical systems, and the wrong power source could leave you stranded.

Most batteries are located up front, under the hood, where they're easy to access and replace with a couple of wrenches. But some are buried in the trunk or elsewhere—not so easy to find, let alone remove and replace.

Just remember, the negative terminal is always the first thing you disconnect and the last thing you reconnect.

Regardless of whether you're doing it in your driveway or letting a shop install, it's a good idea to first make sure you're buying the correct physical size. A number of sizes fit today's wide variety of vehicles.

For instance, size 24/24F (top terminal) batteries fit many Honda, Acura, Toyota, Lexus, Nissan, and Infiniti vehicles, while size 35 (top terminal) units fit many other Japanese vehicles, including recent Toyotas, Nissans, Hondas, and Subarus.

Size 48H6 (top terminal) batteries fit many European and American vehicles. Again, you can find which size you need in your owner's manual, in the replacement guides at the retail store, or online.

Almost all cars come with a 12-volt sealed lead-acid (SLA) battery of some variety (a few high-performance cars are equipped with lithium-ion batteries). These SLA batteries use the same chemistry as the ones your dad had to periodically top off with water, but today they are sealed—hence the name—and maintenance-free.

See all results for used cars for sale near 07011

Absorbent glass mat (AGM) batteries have quickly become the norm for most modern cars. They use similar chemistry as SLAs but are more durable and are claimed to stand up to more charge cycles.

Gel-cell batteries are best for deep discharging but may have problems in extreme hot or cold. Those old "wet cell" batteries from Dad's day are still available, though primarily for older models or penny pinchers. They are likely not offered in the right sizes and specs to support modern cars, however.

The next thing to check is the engine-cranking power of a vehicle battery, which is expressed in cranking amps (CA) and/or cold-cranking amps (CCA), a measure of how much electric current (in amperes) it can deliver for 30 seconds at 32 and zero degrees Fahrenheit. A bigger number is better, especially in cold weather, when batteries are at their weakest.

Another number to understand is the battery's reserve capacity, which is how long it can provide power with the engine off and headlights and/or accessories on or if the vehicle's charging system fails. One and a half hours is good. Two hours is better.

Also important is the warranty, which should be at least three years for full replacement (assuming no signs of neglect or abuse), plus, in some cases, a prorated refund for some time after that. Bear in mind, manufacturer warranties are often not supported when parts and accessories are purchased online from retailers like Amazon or Walmart.

Finally, be forewarned: Some brands, such as BMW, require the battery to be "coded" (digitally mated) to the car or it will not take a charge. Coding the battery requires BMW-specific OBD-II software that any reputable service shop or BMW dealer will have.

Expect to pay anywhere between $100 and $400 for a new battery, with lower-performing SLA types at the low end and stronger, longer-lasting AGMs near the top. If you're having it installed, the shop will dispose of your old battery.

If you're doing it yourself, take your old one to the retail outlet for recycling and to avoid a core charge—a mandatory deposit on your new battery that is refunded when you return the old one. Before you hand it over, place it side by side with the new battery to confirm the one you're buying is the same size. It's a final check to make sure your choice is the right one.

Oh, and if you're taking it home to install, get one with a traveling handle if possible—a car battery can weigh between 25 and 60 pounds.

#4527. Tesla drops car referral rewards, now pays owners in FSD for referrals

Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.

At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.

To share a link, you need to be paying for FSD (Supervised) monthly or own it outright from before Tesla stopped selling it, according to Tesla’s FSD referral support page. Owners who got FSD through a one-year grant can’t participate. The link lives under “Refer and Earn” in the Tesla app, version 4.62.0 or later.

The person on the other end has to own a registered Tesla with compatible hardware, can’t have paid for FSD in the past 12 months, and can’t have bought it outright. There’s also a catch for recent buyers: anyone who got a free FSD trial with a new car is locked out of referral links until 12 months after that trial ends.

The bigger change is buried in Tesla’s Refer and Earn page. Buyer benefits now apply to solar panels only. Referrer benefits cover solar, first demo drives (up to 30 over an account’s lifetime) and the new FSD referral.

Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck only show up under loyalty benefits, for existing owners buying another Tesla product. Model S and Model X aren’t listed at all.

Tesla didn’t announce the change. The page is stamped “Updated February 24, 2026,” so it’s unclear exactly when vehicles came off the list.

That’s quite a turn for a program that was always about moving cars. When Tesla brought the referral program back in August 2024, a buyer got $1,000 off a Model S, X, Y or 3, and the referrer got $500 in credit. Tesla has killed and revived the program several times over the past decade, but cars were always at the center of it. Not anymore.

That’s the exact metric in Elon Musk’s 2025 CEO Performance Award, which includes a milestone of 10 million active FSD subscriptions. It’s the reason Tesla started disclosing the number in January in the first place.

The free month a friend receives doesn’t count toward that total. A paid conversion does, and that’s precisely the event the new program pays for.

The only way I would ever pay for FSD is if Tesla covered full comprehensive insurance for my vehicle and accepted all liability. Otherwise, it's a gamble with my (and others') life.

That they seem to prioritize this sham service (Just call it Assisted Driving for honesty sake?) versus improving the cars or lowering prices, tells me enough not to look at Tesla for my next vehicle.

The recipient has to already own a Tesla, so the program doesn’t add a single car to the fleet. It’s built to mine the existing fleet for subscriptions. Tesla had sold about 8.9 million vehicles by the end of 2025, and only 1.74 million are paying for FSD, so there’s plenty of room. At Q3’s pace, we estimated 10 million subscriptions is still about eight years away.

So Tesla stopped paying for referrals that require selling a car, and started paying for the ones that move the number in Musk’s pay package. We think that tells you a lot about where the company’s priorities are right now.

#4525. This Startup Is Turning Used E-Bike Batteries Into Affordable Energy Storage

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Millions of e-bike and e-scooter batteries are thrown away every year, even though they might still have life in them. Now, a German startup is trying to reduce battery waste by integrating used batteries from e-mobility vehicles into energy storage systems.

EDENenergy, which has just three part-time staff members in addition to its three founders, has shipped its first commercial product, a 70-kilowatt-hour battery system that uses no fewer than 112 second-life e-scooter batteries.

All modules were thoroughly tested, and the results were better than expected. The company’s founders, who used to be researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE, said that they expected the old batteries to have roughly 80% life left in them, but the tests revealed that most retained about 90% of their original capacity.

After being abused in their previous life, the e-scooter batteries will have a much easier future in the startup’s energy storage systems, where vibrations and large temperature fluctuations are non-existent. What’s more, the long-term energy capacity of the system can be easily kept at 70 kWh by simply replacing modules that become unusable down the line.

The startup said it remotely monitors each module, and when it’s time for a replacement, it can be done without powering down the whole system. That’s a big plus, especially for energy-sensitive scenarios where cutting the power would result in massive losses.

The keen-eyed among you might have noticed that there’s a solar inverter on one side of the battery box. That’s because EDENenergy’s first product was designed for companies that have solar panels but can’t store solar energy yet. “In mid-October, we delivered the first storage system to a customer, which was an important milestone for our young company,” said Florian Bierwirth, one of the founders. “With this storage size, we initially aim to target medium-sized companies in the region that have a photovoltaic system but do not yet have a storage solution.”

For its next step, the startup wants to come up with a way of using different batteries from different manufacturers. “To do this, the connector interfaces, battery management system, and communication protocols must be adapted for each new battery. There’s a particularly wide range of options when it comes to e-bikes,” said Bierwirth. Currently, the small company relies on large suppliers that can send in large numbers of the same battery type.

A larger-capacity battery system of up to 300 kWh is also in the works, putting roughly 500 second-life e-scooter modules to good use instead of sending them to the landfill. The batteries will eventually give up, but when that happens, they’ll be sent to a recycling facility where they’ll be dismantled, and their contents will be reused, if possible.

#4522. EVs Made Up Nearly A Third Of UK Sales As Europe's Electric Boom Continues

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

While EV sales are growing slowly in the U.S., despite the loss of federal tax incentives, they're exploding in the UK. According to UK's car industry lobby New Automotive, 49,155 new fully battery-electric vehicles (BEV) were sold in October. That's not only a massive 54% increase over last October, but it's 32% of the UK's new car market share, or almost a third.

That 32% market share also gave EVs the largest market share of any one fuel type, more than gas, diesel, or hybrids. "Almost one in three new cars sold in October was fully electric, more than any other fuel type, and electric car sales are up by more than half on last year," said Ben Nelmes, CEO at New AutoMotive. "Drivers are voting with their wallets. Every one of those new electric cars means a household spending less on running costs, and a country less exposed to the oil price shock."

There's more EV variety in the UK than there is in America. The UK has access to EVs from brands like Renault, Peugeot, Fiat, Volkswagen, Skoda, and even Chinese EVs like BYD and Jaecoo. Last month, Kia, BMW, Volkswagen, and BYD led the country's electric market. Tesla slumped after a big September.

Year-to-date, though, Tesla is number one, with 9.53% market share. That's up 25.4% from last year, too. Kia took second place, with 6.9% market share, and BYD came in third, with 6.8%. What's surprising is that no European EV brands were in the top three, despite being in their home continent. I'd sell a non-essential organ for a Renault 5 E-Tech, so I'm surprised to see cars like that not taking top spots in the UK.

It isn't just new EVs, either. The UK is also seeing a jump in used EVs, just like we are here. According to EV Powered, data shows that more and more UK customers are shopping for used EVs.

The run up in oil costs is driving record EV sales across Europe. BEVs took 37% share of the car market in Germany, the country's road traffic agency said, with over 94,000 vehicles sold. That's a nearly 80% increase year over year.

#4520. BYD reveals a flashy new feature on its upcoming luxury EV

BYD is moving upmarket with its new flagship EV, featuring suicide doors, a gemstone grille, and possibly solid-state batteries.

Yangwang is like BMW’s Rolls-Royce and Mercedes-Maybach, sitting at the very top of BYD’s brand hierarchy.

The ultra-luxury brand offers BYD’s most high-end and technically advanced vehicles, including the U7 sedan, the U8, a hardcore off-road SUV, and the U9, an electric supercar.

Yangwang vehicles have previously debuted with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including its quad-motor e4 platform (delivering over 1,300 hp), its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging, and its DiSus-X intelligent body control system.

Its next model will push further into the elite segment. After BYD revealed the name of its new flagship executive sedan earlier this week, the Yangwang Altior, the company has released several new details ahead of its official debut.

Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing confirmed on Friday that the new Yangwang Altior will feature suicide doors, a first for a BYD model.

The new door design swings open nearly 90 degrees, Hu said, creating a dramatic, wide-open entrance.

Hu also posted a preview of the vehicle’s front fascia, complete with a dot-matrix Gemstrone grille and crystal-inspired headlights.

BYD has not confirmed many details, but the ultra-luxury sedan is expected to be about 5,500 mm (216″) in length.

Images of the disguised vehicle released last month show a similar shape and size to the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class or Rolls-Royce Phantom.

HU said last week that the global launch of the new flagship sedan will take place in the UAE, not in BYD’s home market of China.

BYD has not revealed an official date, but according to CarNewsChina, citing “sources familiar with the project,” BYD aims to unveil the new flagship model in Dubai, UAE, around November 5.

The Yangwang Altrio will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, said.

In one image, the vehicle was charging at a BYD Flash Charge station, suggesting it will use its Blade Battery 2.0 and 5-minute Flash Charging technology.

There are companies showcasing flying cars designed specifically for circus-style shows, while others are launching solid-state batteries that can recharge in five minutes.

I find myself wondering—though perhaps not too deeply—which of these technologies will secure the largest customer base and generate the greatest returns for shareholders.

Outside of the suicide doors, rumors suggest the flagship model will be BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries. Executive vice president Stella Li said during an interview with Carwow.es last month that BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries will debut in 2027.

The executive sedan is expected to debut around November 5. Prices are rumored to start in the 2 million yuan range, or about $300,000.

Yangwang’s current electric sedan, the U7, starts at 658,000 yuan ($98,000). The extended U8L, on the other hand, is the brand’s highest-priced mass-produced vehicle, starting at 1.45 million yuan ($217,000).

#4519. China Has An Iron Grip On EV Batteries. Here's America’s Plan To Break It

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The U.S. Department of Energy last week released a new three-step plan to localize the supply chain of batteries and reduce America’s reliance on China. The plan may not even mention electric vehicles, but the EV market could be among its biggest beneficiaries if successfully executed.

Citing data from research firm BloombergNEF, the DOE said demand for batteries would increase four fold between 2025 and 2035, from 179 gigawatt-hours to 707 GWh. The demand is expected to skyrocket across sectors including transportation, the power grid, AI data centers, consumer electronics, and drones.

While the report acknowledged that America’s battery cell and pack manufacturing had improved over the past few years, the core supply chain was still heavily reliant on imports. That means things like raw material mining and the production of a battery’s subcomponents such as anodes, cathodes, electrolytes, and separators were still largely happening overseas, mostly in China.

To fix this, DOE said a new three-step plan was necessary, and the following are its objectives:

In part one of this plan, the focus would be to invest in the battery supply chain. “DOE is prioritizing investments to shift from a discontinuous, import-reliant supply chain to an integrated domestic production system through the upstream (mining), midstream (refining and engineered materials), and downstream (cells, packs, and end products),” the DOE said. It added that it would focus on targeted investments in companies that specialize in extraction, recycling, refining, and equipment manufacturing.

Part two outlines developing and commercializing next-generation batteries that are right for their specific applications. “These batteries should be more affordable, longer lasting, higher performing, and less reliant on critical minerals in select market segments,” the DOE said. So think solid-state cells or more advanced versions of current lithium-ion technology. And the final part of the plan is to get them past the “valley of death,” meaning converting discoveries made in the lab into actual products people can buy.

To be clear, the Biden administration had shared similar objectives back in 2021 in far more detail with a focus on clean energy, social justice, and equitable jobs. The Trump administration’s blueprint is much thinner and instead leans on national security, the grid, humanoid robots, and the enormous power demands of AI data centers. It doesn't explicitly mention EVs, but instead says next-gen batteries would also help in the transportation sector.

It's also worth remembering that America's battery industry was surging long before that. After Trump swept to power in 2024, battery manufacturing in the U.S. took a severe hit. According to clean energy think tank E2, the U.S. canceled, closed or downsized battery projects worth $42 billion between 2022 and 2026, costing the nation over 85,000 jobs. Across the broader clean energy sector, the sum increases to $137 billion, costing over 240,000 jobs, according to the same report.

The new blueprint is still a step in the right direction, even if it is more of a continued effort. It also reflects how much the battery landscape has changed since the start of the decade. EV sales have been up and down, while demand for stationary energy storage has surged, driven by utility upgrades and AI data centers. The revised strategy accounts for that shift, and automakers could still benefit over the long term for their EV plans.

#4518. Honda has dominated motorcycles for decades. Electric bikes are changing that

Honda has spent decades building one of the most dominant positions in the global motorcycle industry, selling millions of gasoline-powered two-wheelers each year. But in markets where electric motorcycles and scooters are becoming increasingly accessible, that dominance is starting to face a serious challenge.

Vietnam offers a particularly interesting case study, where rapidly growing electric motorcycle sales are beginning to reshape a market long dominated by Honda.

According to newly released nationwide sales figures, Vietnam saw more than 3 million motorcycle and scooter sales during the first nine months of 2026, representing 25.9% growth over the same period last year.

But the real story is in the electric segment, where sales surged 90.5% to reach 973,247 units. That means electric two-wheelers now account for approximately 32% of all new motorcycle and scooter sales in the country.

And the biggest beneficiary isn’t Honda. It’s actually Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer VinFast.

While Honda remains Vietnam’s largest motorcycle manufacturer overall, with sales growing 8.4% this year, VinFast has surged into second place with a staggering 152.1% increase in sales. Yamaha now sits in third place, followed by electric two-wheeler manufacturer Yadea in fourth.

Of the top four players, half are electric, and it’s precisely that half that is experiencing meteoric sales growth.

It’s an impressive reshuffling of a market that has traditionally been dominated by Japanese gasoline motorcycle manufacturers.

Vietnam’s transition hasn’t happened in a vacuum, either. Government efforts to reduce urban air pollution, including plans to restrict gasoline-powered motorcycles in parts of Hanoi, have helped create an increasingly favorable environment for electric alternatives.

Too bad for Honda but I'm thrilled to read about increasing sales of electric motorcycles. I don't live in or near Vietnam but the pollution from small gasoline engines affects everyone where the wind blows it.

And with companies like VinFast offering an expanding range of electric scooters and motorcycles, riders now have more practical alternatives to gasoline-powered models than ever before.

To be clear, Honda isn’t exactly struggling. Its motorcycle sales are still growing, and the Japanese giant remains the undisputed market leader in Vietnam. But its overall share of the market is shrinking, and its relatively modest growth compared to the exploding electric segment suggests that the market’s center of gravity is beginning to shift.

Vietnam may be just a single example, but it’s an important one of what can happen when electric two-wheelers become viable mainstream alternatives to gasoline motorcycles.

Honda has spent decades perfecting the gasoline motorcycle. The question now is how quickly it can adapt to a market that is increasingly interested in something else.

#4517. Uber Wants Thousands Of Robotaxis By 2027. Waymo Is Already There

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Uber has racked up a ton of autonomous vehicle partnerships, attempting to position itself as the key platform for driverless rides. And the company has no plans to slow down. On Tuesday, Uber said it wants to spend $10 billion to get 2,000 robotaxis into its global fleet by the end of 2027.

"Our autonomous strategy is entering an important new phase as more of our partners move from development and testing into driverless commercial service," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in written remarks shared alongside the company's third-quarter earnings.

Around half of those 2,000 robotaxis will be for the United States market, Uber said. The other half will be split up between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Uber says the self-driving fleet at that point will span 20 cities and include partnerships with May Mobility, Momenta, Zoox, Motional, and others. By the end of this year, Uber plans to have 700 robotaxis on its platform.

Here's the kicker, though: Even if Uber hits its goal by 2027, it will still be far behind Waymo, which is both a major competitor and, for now, a partner. Waymo, the most prominent robotaxi company in the world, already has a fleet of around 4,000 cars currently on the road, and it currently operates in 15 different U.S. cities.

Waymo aims to double its robotaxi count to 8,000 by the end of the year and hit 20,000 vehicles by the close of 2027, Semafor reported recently. So Uber would still be playing catch-up, big time.

And while users in cities like Atlanta have to use the Uber app to call a Waymo robotaxi, that's changing. Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg on Wednesday that the company plans to end its exclusivity deal with Uber in Austin and Atlanta in January of 2028. It was “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, since Uber customers never knew if they were getting a robotaxi or a human driver.

Uber said its partners have committed to bringing 120,000 robotaxis onto its platform in the coming years, but hasn't put a timeframe on such a lofty goal. It says it's going to fund this fleet of robotaxis with its own earnings, but that it might have to “bring in third-party capital," once its self-driving fleet expands beyond 10,000 cars. Uber claims its gross bookings were up 20%, year-over-year, to the tune of $59.8 billion, so it's got a big book of business to fund its future projects. But with it splitting from Waymo, it's never been more important for the company to get its other partnership projects off the ground and expand them quickly.

#4515. I imported a $2,000 electric truck from China. Five years later, here’s the truth

Five years ago, I did something that seemed pretty ridiculous at the time. I bought a $2,000 electric mini-truck from China, had it shipped across the oceans to the US, and put it to work on my parents’ property in Florida.

The little white mini electric truck became something of an internet sensation, with my original unboxing and testing video quickly racking up over 10 million views, plus several million more from the follow-up videos.

It also attracted plenty of skeptics who were convinced that a $2,000 Chinese electric truck would fall apart within months, rust into oblivion, or otherwise prove to be a spectacular waste of money. “Good thing it has a bed,” was a common refrain. “So you can collect all the pieces that fall off along the way.”

I gave an update after the first year, showing that the truck was doing great. But to be fair, one year doesn’t tell us much.

Well now it’s been over five years, and I recently returned to Florida to see how the little truck has held up after five trips around the sun on my parents’ homestead. And I’ve got to say, the results are pretty surprising.

So here’s the truth about how the truck is doing five years later. Oh, and if you want to see it in action, you can check out my update video here. Trust me, you’ll want to.

First, it’s important to understand that this truck hasn’t spent five years sitting in a garage as some kind of novelty vehicle. It’s been a genuine workhorse on my parents’ 10-acre homestead.

Over the years, we’ve used it to haul everything from mulch and sand to lumber, tree branches, logs, yard waste, and everything in between.

Its hydraulic dump bed makes it particularly useful for moving bulk materials around the property, like hauling mulch and then dumping it in their raised planting beds.

My dad even uses it as a mobile irrigation truck during Florida’s dry season. I built him a solar-powered pump system that fills a water bladder in the truck’s bed with water from his pond, allowing him to drive around watering his trees and plants.

By now, it’s been involved in practically every major landscaping and construction project my parents have tackled.

We’ve also made some improvements over the years. Early on, my dad and I replaced the ridiculously stiff factory suspension springs with softer ones, making the ride considerably more comfortable. We added a custom tow hitch and swapped the original street tires for aggressive off-road tires that work much better on the property’s sandy and muddy terrain.

The suspension upgrade did reduce how much weight we can comfortably carry, though. Load more than around 500 pounds (220 kg) of sand or other bulk materials into the bed, and the rear end starts squatting enough that our homemade tow hitch threatens to touch grass.

But for most of the work we do, it’s been an excellent little utility vehicle.

And before anyone asks, no, this isn’t a street-legal truck. It was never really designed for American roads, and we use it almost exclusively on private property. Sure, it’s hit the pavement a few times since they live out in the boonies and its normal to see tractors and other non-street-legal vehicles on country roads, but it’s not the most ideal vehicle for long distance transport at 25 mph (40 km/h).

Here’s the part that surprised me most: Almost everything still works.

The electric windows still zip up and down with the speed of a guillotine. The electric door locks work. The headlights work. The backup camera works. Even the air conditioning still blows impressively cold air.

I actually checked that last one with a thermal camera during my latest visit, and the air coming out of the vents was around 55°F (12°C). Not bad for a five-year-old air conditioning system in a $2,000 truck!

The windshield wiper still operates, but its range of motion has decreased significantly. It now stops around the middle of the driver’s field of vision, which isn’t ideal when Florida’s famous afternoon thunderstorms roll through.

The rearview mirror has also developed an annoying habit of falling off. We’ve glued it back on multiple times, and it looks like another round of adhesive surgery is coming soon.

Inside, there’s some minor upholstery damage on the driver’s seat, including a few small tears and stressed seams in the cheap faux-leather material that you can see in the video.

The passenger seat, which sees much less use, still looks nearly new. In another few years, I might just swap the two seats to get another half decade or so out of them before we need some upholstery repair.

One decorative plastic panel around the driver’s door handle has popped off, though I still have the piece and could probably snap it back into place with a bit of effort. It’s just aesthetic though, so it’s been a low-priority repair.

And that’s pretty much the extent of the mechanical and electrical problems we’ve encountered.

There haven’t been any major drivetrain failures, the hydraulic dump bed still works, and the truck continues to start up and drive just as reliably as it did when it was new.

It still gets used for lots of bulk jobs, material hauling, and sometimes just random transportation around the property.

One of the biggest predictions from critics five years ago was that this cheap Chinese truck would quickly dissolve into a pile of rust.

To be fair, there is some rust. But nowhere near as much as you might expect.

Most of the corrosion is concentrated in areas where the paint has been scratched or chipped, especially around the tailgate and cargo bed.

The rustiest spot is definitely the top lip of the tailgate, where we usually have long objects hanging out of the bed, such as shovels, ladders, lumber, etc. The paint has worn through on that edge, and the rust has inevitably started in those few spots.

The truck is stored outdoors under a lean-to roof that I built between two shipping containers, but we have a skid-steer in front of it and so the rear of the truck sticks out and gets rained on several times a week (or several times a day during the summer).

We applied a paint-on bed liner during the truck’s first year, which helped protect the metal for quite a while.

After four years of hauling dirt, rocks, branches, and other abrasive materials though, that coating has started wearing through in a few places.

Every time I’m shoveling mulch out of the bed and I hear that scrape of metal on metal, I cringe just a bit before remembering that the truck cost me $2,000 and doesn’t owe me anything at this point.

Speaking of being parked outdoors with the rear hanging out for the world (and the UV) to see, there’s clearly an effect on the truck’s wear.

You can absolutely see the difference in the paint and plastic components. The front headlight lenses are still crystal clear, while the rear taillight lenses have become noticeably cloudy from UV exposure.

Despite that, the truck’s basic structure remains solid, and the rust is mostly cosmetic and limited to the high-impact areas that tend to get beaten up repeatedly, as you’d expect in any self-respecting work truck.

Considering that Florida combines high humidity, frequent rain, and intense sunshine, I’d call that a pretty impressive result for a vehicle that cost less than many electric bicycles.

Since the truck lives at my parents’ property, my dad has actually spent far more time using it than I have.

And when I asked him how he felt about the purchase after five years, he was surprisingly enthusiastic.

He described the truck as an incredibly functional piece of equipment that has become an essential part of maintaining the property.

In fact, he pointed out that the truck has been involved in virtually every significant project they’ve completed over the past five years.

It isn’t the only electric utility vehicle on the property anymore. My parents also have a Kandi electric UTV, which has taken over some of the smaller daily chores thanks to its better suspension and more convenient dump bed operation (the bed also lowers under power) which helps my dad lift the trash and recycling bins and drive them down the long private road to the street on pickup day.

But when it’s time to haul bulky loads, long branches, or large quantities of dirt and mulch, the Changli is still the vehicle of choice.

My dad also pointed out something that tends to get lost in discussions about cheap Chinese EVs: the operating costs have been almost nonexistent.

A full charge costs a little over a dollar in electricity, and the truck has required remarkably little maintenance over the years.

Even after five years, he says it still puts a smile on his face every time he drives it.

Yes, the truck cost me $2,000. Or technically, the price was $2,080.00, and that’s what I paid to the factory. At that point, it was mine.

Of course, it was still in China though, and so I had to pay an international freight company to have it sent on a cargo ship to the US (nearly $2,000 by itself, if I recall correctly).

Then I had to pay the US Treasury a bunch of tariffs to help make sure American automotive companies don’t have to compete with these types of vehicles.

And I also had to hire a customs broker to handle the import documentation for me, etc.

So there were several thousand dollars of additional fees on top of it, but I still think it was worth it based on the incredible amount of use it has given us over the years.

Of course, there’s an important caveat here for anyone considering getting a vehicle like this.

Remember, this is a very basic, low-speed electric utility vehicle without the safety equipment, crash protection, or regulatory approvals you’d expect from a modern full-size pickup truck.

It’s not something I’d recommend as a replacement for a road-going vehicle.

This is a work truck for us. It moves material, tows trailers and boats, carries the trash cans a quarter mile to the street each week, etc. In that way, as a private-property work truck, it’s been fantastic.

But even though I’m calling it simple, that doesn’t mean it wasn’t made pretty well. The truck has hauled countless loads, survived five years of rough Florida weather, and required very little maintenance. Even its cheap interior and basic electronics have held up better than I expected.

I also have to give some credit to the modifications we made early on, especially the suspension and tire upgrades, which turned a quirky little imported vehicle into something much more practical for off-road work.

The biggest unknown is how much longer it will last. Unfortunately, the truck doesn’t have a proper odometer, so I can’t even tell you how many miles we’ve accumulated over five years of driving around the property.

I also can’t tell you anything about battery degradation, since we don’t know how far it has driven (due to the lack of odometer), and the fact that even on 10 acres, you just can’t get that far from an outlet. We generally charge the 6 kWh battery every couple weeks just to keep it topped up, but range was never an issue and hasn’t become one, at least not for our use case. If you needed to drive this thing to the next town over each day, it could be another story.

Nothing like being forced to drive massive four-door trucks that weigh as much as four cars because your country is protecting monopolist manufacturers and only allows their land yachts for sale.

Basically, there’s no indication that the mini-truck is nearing the end of its useful life.

My dad thinks it could easily serve another five or even ten years, and after seeing how well it’s survived its first five, I’m inclined to agree that there’s plenty of life left in it.

When I first bought this thing, plenty of people told me it was a terrible idea. Five years later, with the truck still hauling dirt, carrying branches, and generally earning its keep, I’m feeling pretty good about that decision. It’s done a lot more in its five years than many “real” pickup trucks do in their entire lives.

Not bad for a funny little electric truck from China.

#4514. Speeders just got lucky: the new Chevy police Silverado is NOT electric

Say what you will about America’s police forces, but they are loyal – often to each other, and always to their preferred brand of pursuit vehicle. And if the thin blue line of Chevy faithful won’t embrace the 750 hp electric Silverado because it’s powered by batteries, that can really only be called a win for the scofflaws they’re pursuing.

A new 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 9C1 police pursuit vehicle (PPV) was on display in the GM Fleet booth at the Orange County Convention Center this past week, where the new half-ton was featured fitted a new, 402 hp version of the venerable 5.7 small-block Chevy V8 sending 428 lb-ft of torque to both axles through a 10-speed automatic transmission. The 9C1 also features an available 2″ lift kit that retains the truck’s pursuit rating, up to 9,300 lbs. of towing capacity, and an available driver’s side LED spotlight.

If that all sounds somewhat pedestrian, it might be because Electrek readers are more familiar with the Silverado EV, which offers more than 750 hp in WOW mode and 775 lb-ft of torque at 0 rpm, along with a pessimistic EPA rating of just 478 miles – which, hilariously, is about the same “range” as the 16 mpg (combined) gas version, despite the EV packing nearly 350 additional horsepower, the ability to cruise in silence, and the significantly reduced maintenance and total cost of ownership costs of going electric.

Which, I guess, are all reasonably obvious things that nobody actually asked me about – and certainly nobody with a criminal justice degree and a statistically low LSAT score, so I’ll get back to talking about the truck, itself.

A massive, 16″ touchscreen display dominates the interior of the PPV, and was also touted as a standard feature (as it across Chevy’s civilian line), though if and how it would integrate with police department software isn’t clear – and my guess is that enforcement computing will continue to be an upfitter issue.

I don’t know why anyone would use a truck as a persuit vehicle? It seems reckless inefficient and ineffective.

Guess we are on the topic of us policing…

#4513. Waymo And Uber's Robotaxi Partnership Is Ending

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

If you want to ride in a driverless Waymo in Austin or Atlanta, you can currently only do that via the Uber app thanks to an exclusive partnership between the two companies. That will change in 2028 because Waymo has decided to go solo in those two cities.

Waymo Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg on Wednesday that the company will exit its partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta starting in January 2028. The reason? Mawakana said the Uber app doesn’t guarantee a driverless ride. You can enable autonomous rides via settings in the Uber app, but the chances of one showing up depend on how many Waymos are actually nearby. If there's no Waymo nearby, riders are matched with human drivers.

Uber says it offered to add a dedicated robotaxi ride option through its service so that customers would match with driverless cars more easily, but Waymo reportedly declined that.

“In the early days, we would partner because we didn’t have the scale,” Mawakana told the outlet. "...in that partnering, it was a little bit of a crapshoot," she added.

Customers were now demanding a more consistent experience, Mawakana said. That’s why, starting in January 2028, Waymos in Austin and Atlanta will operate the same way they’ve been operating in over two dozen other U.S. cities: via Waymo’s own dedicated app. With that, current partner Uber will also become a direct rival in those two cities.

The whole point of this partnership was to help Waymo scale and give riders exposure to its cutting-edge driverless technology. Uber is the go-to ride-hail app for millions of riders already. The company also has vast experience in fleet operations and logistics.

Waymo, by comparison, is far smaller but is growing quickly. It’s a fully-owned subsidiary of Google parent Alphabet, which is valued at over $3.5 trillion as of writing. Waymo currently conducts over 500,000 paid driverless trips each week. It’s already operational in 15 U.S. cities and plans to add over a dozen more in the coming months. It's in a comfortable lead in the robotaxi race in the U.S., far ahead of Tesla and others.

It now seems more confident about going solo in Austin and Atlanta. However, it’s still partnering with Lyft for driverless rides in Nashville, although that partnership isn’t exclusive. Waymo also serves Nashville through its own app.

Uber also has grand ambitions when it comes to robotaxis. The company plans to have 700 robotaxis online by the end of this year and 2,000 by the end of 2027. It has emerged as a broker of robotaxi technology, inking deals with several companies including Rivian, Lucid, Wayve, and others to offer their driverless vehicles on the Uber app.

#4512. Nissan Turns the Armada into the Safari-Ready Jungle Patrol Concept

The Armada Jungle Patrol loses its roof, rides on a custom long-travel suspension, and wears tubular bumpers and lots of auxiliary lighting.

Each year, the SEMA show in Las Vegas allows automakers to let their creativity shine through custom concepts based on production vehicles. In 2025, Nissan turned its full-size Armada SUV into the desert-ready Dune Patrol, adding a long-travel suspension, unique bumpers, and a durable roof rack. Now, for 2026, Nissan has modified the Armada once again, this time transforming it into the Jungle Patrol, ripping off the roof to make the SUV into the ideal safari companion.

The Armada Jungle Patrol’s biggest change is, obviously, the lack of a roof, with the solid shelter replaced by a tubular roll cage, providing a better view of the natural world you’re exploring. Just be ready to speed away if a lion gets a little too curious about the tasty treats sitting inside. The rear section has been fitted with inward-facing bench seats, a common setup in safari vehicles.

See all results for new 2026 Nissan Armada for sale near 98837

Nissan also upgraded the Armada to tackle more serious terrain. The Jungle Patrol rides on prototype 18-inch NISMO wheels wrapped in 37-inch Yokohama Geolandar G003 M/T tires, which are suspended on a custom long-travel setup from CJD Racing. The setup utilizes high-performance adjustable coil-overs with remote reservoirs and bypass, and the Jungle Patrol has a wider track than the regular Armada.

The Jungle Patrol is also equipped with custom steel bumpers and fender flares, and there are NISMO off-road lights mounted on the bumper and roof to illuminate the jungle at night. Nissan caps off the look with a unique livery, which reads “Jungle Patrol” in a scrawled font and features what look like the claw marks of some intimidating jungle beast down the rear doors.

As with the Desert Patrol last year, Nissan has left the standard 425-hp twin-turbo 3.5-liter V-6 engine untouched but added a custom NISMO cat-back exhaust. While the Armada Jungle Patrol is a fun experiment, we assume it will never enter production given its extreme mission, but some features, like the prototype wheels and custom bumpers, could one day be offered as official NISMO aftermarket parts.

#4511. Bigger, badder Section 179 tax deduction could POWER UP fleet electrification [update]

With national diesel prices inching towards $7/gallon and Tesla’s $290,000 Semi trucks finally making their way to paying customers, it’s worth revisiting how Trump’s One Big, Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) helped beef up the Section 179 deduction, and look again at how it could help your fleet ditch diesel sooner rather than later.

At the core of this thinking is the fact that the IRS does not distinguish between fuel choices, so there’s no separate depreciation category for electric- vs. diesel-fueled commercial trucks. The relevant classifications, then, are the vehicle’s use and property classes, and under the IRS’ depreciation guidelines, tractor units designed for over-the-road use are classified as 3-year properties and fall under the 20-year recovery threshold for 100% bonus depreciation, Tesla’s electric Semi can benefit from 179 just like their diesel-powered competitors. But don’t get me wrong – this isn’t just great news for Tesla Semi buyers. Electric garbage trucks, electric vocational trucks, battery electric reefer trailers, and even some big electric forklifts can potentially benefit from the same accelerated depreciation rules, since the IRS lists these as, “specialized business vehicles,” with no distinction between electric, diesel, natural gas, hydrogen, magic pixie dust, anything else.

There’s been some additional movement on the tax front since our original article, too. Earlier this year, the IRS issued Notice 2026-11, providing additional guidance on the permanent restoration of 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying property acquired after January 19, 2025. That means that eligible businesses might be able to combine Section 179 expensing with bonus depreciation when ordering qualifying fleet equipment – and ordering is the key word. The IRS has specific rules for determining when equipment is considered acquired under a written, binding contract, and your tax professional and truck dealer can probably help you figure out a way to make those rules work in your favor.

You can check out the original article (with a few corrections sprinkled in to align with the latest guidance from Notice 2026-11 and Publication 946) below. Give it a read, read the disclaimer twice, then let us know what you think in the comments.

After the Commercial Clean Vehicle Credit (Section 45W) expired on September 30, the “experts” rushed out predictions of an EV sales slowdown in Q4. But, with over 6,800 pages in the Internal Revenue Code still in play, a turbocharged Section 179 tax deduction could still power a strong year for commercial EVs.

The One Big, Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) of 2025 gutted America’s energy independence goals and ensuring its auto industry would fall even further behind the Chinese in the EV race, but the loss of Section 45W wasn’t the only change written into the IRS’ rulebook. Section 179, an immediate expense reduction that business owners can take on depreciable equipment assets, has been made significantly more powerful for 2025.

The section 179 expense deduction is limited to such items as cars, office equipment, business machinery, and computers. This speedy deduction can provide substantial tax relief for business owners who are purchasing startup equipment.

The revised Section 179 tax credit (or, more accurately, expense reduction) allows for a 100% deduction for equipment purchases has doubled to $2.5 million, with a phase-out kicking in at $4 million of capital investments that drops to zero at $6.5 million. That can be applied to new and used vehicles, as well as charging infrastructure, battery energy storage systems, specialized tools, and more (as long as they’re new to you).

“But wait,” as they say. “There’s more!” A revised Section 168(k) also allows for bonus depreciation on eligible equipment and property, accelerating depreciation for a reduced tax burden.

Section 179 and bonus depreciation aren’t mutually exclusive, either, which means that businesses don’t have to exceed the Section 179 spending cap to be able to take advantage of both. A fleet operator can elect to expense a portion of a qualifying vehicle or equipment purchase under Section 179, then apply bonus depreciation to the remaining eligible basis.

With 100% bonus depreciation restored for qualifying property acquired after January 19, 2025, that combination could allow businesses to deduct the entire qualifying business-use cost of an electric truck or other commercial equipment in the first year, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and limitations.

It’s a bit convoluted (what good tax code isn’t?), but these tax incentives are great for businesses looking to buy enough electric equipment assets to exceed the Section 179 spending limit – and, given the new Uber/Tesla semi truck purchase plan, the continued growth of the electric terminal tractor market, and the willingness of several utilities to incentivize both electric commercial vehicles and the deployment of smart EV charging infrastructure, that number may be bigger than you think.

Tax law is weird. Not only are there Federal tax laws and rules that need to be followed, but state and even local county and city rules, as well. As such, you want to make sure they don’t get you the way the got Capone.

Even worse, your favorite journalist (Hi!) is probably an idiot. Get a certified accountant and tax law expert to help walk you through the dirtier details of your specific scenario – but don’t let the complexity of human interaction slow you down, either. The really rich guys you know pay pennies on the tax dollar compared to you and me, because they’re not afraid to ask their accountants for help.

As a tax CPA, I cringe when I see "Sec 179" and the word "credit" put together. It is grossly inaccurate to say that Sec 179 is a tax credit.

Sec 179 and bonus depreciation are nothing new. OBBBA just raised the 179 maximum up, but the deductibility, specifically for heavy vehicles like semis, is unchanged.

The TL;DR version, though, is this: there’s still plenty of incentives out there for fleet operators looking to electrify their operations.

#4510. Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Review: Absolute Kaiju Chaos

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered delivers chaotic kaiju battles and couch co-op fun, even if its story and side features are thin.

72 years ago, the world was first introduced to the King of the Monsters, Godzilla, in the revolutionary 1954 kaiju film simply titled Godzilla, and since then the reptilian monster has gone on to appear in dozens of movies, shows, comics, and even video games.

While most of Godzilla’s video game appearances debuted in the 1980s and 1990s, the radioactive monster has made a few notable gaming manifestations in the early 2000s and 2010s, with a fan-favorite being 2002’s Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee.

Godzilla: DAMM turned out to be such a popular sixth generation console title that it not only spawned two sequels but a complete Unreal Engine 5 remaster for modern platforms called Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered.

Looking for new fighting games in 2026? Here are 10 upcoming fighters to watch, including indie gems, arena brawlers, and Godzilla.

To give a little bit of a background on myself with this title, I have never actually played the original Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee before nor any Godzilla game for that matter. I didn’t become a fan of or really understand Godzilla’s cultural importance until high school, around the time when Legendary Pictures’ Godzilla film was coming out coinciding with the franchise’s 60th anniversary.

The success of that film and its later Monsterverse sequels opened the door for me and a whole new generation of fans to become invested in Godzilla and his related kaiju, and seemingly to help capitalize on this new fan base, Atari and Pipeworks have decided to remaster DAMM for modern platforms.

Unlike other remasters, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered isn’t a simple HD port of the original 2002 game but is rather a sort of remake of the original, with Pipeworks having rebuilt the game in Unreal Engine 5 complete with enhanced visuals and modern quality of life improvements.

Pipeworks strived to keep Remastered’s core premise and gameplay as close to the original 2002 game as possible, with the remaster still featuring up to four-player local co-op, Adventure Mode, Destruction Mode, Survival Mode, and Practice Mode.

Pipeworks strived to keep Remastered’s core premise and gameplay as close to the original 2002 game as possible

For the first time ever, Remastered allows DAMM players to fight and play together across great distances thanks to the introduction of online multiplayer.

The game even features updated cutscenes primarily seen in Adventure Mode, with the cutscenes featuring the alien Vortaak being fairly reminiscent of the updated cutscenes in the 2020 Destroy All Humans! remake, especially with how both utilized 1950s-inspired sci-fi movie music.

The premise of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the alien Vortaak have come to Earth and mind-controlled most of the planet’s kaiju to wreck the planet and prepare it for a complete Vortaak invasion. One monster is somehow able to break free of the Vortaak’s control and sets out to defeat all of the other monsters and ultimately the Vortaak themselves.

This storyline is primarily depicted in the remaster’s Adventure Mode, with players being able to select from 12 monsters to play as including:

All of these monsters previously appeared in the original Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee save for the first version of Mechagodzilla who replaced Mechagodzilla 2 in the remaster.

1990s Godzilla, Anguirus, Megalon, and Gigan are all available to play as from the get-go while every other monster has to be unlocked by progressing through G-Force Research Rumors and Projects (not to be confused with the 2009 guinea pig spy movie G-Force).

At the game’s core, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is primarily centered around sandbox fights between two, three, or four monsters, with each monster featuring their own unique moveset that they can use to fight other monsters, destroy cities, and wipe out military units.

These fighting games' story modes allow people to play as villains instead of traditional heroes, often with destructive results.

For example, Megalon can use his drill-like front appendages to not only strike at enemies and buildings but also to burrow underground to pop back up at enemies and unleash a devastating blow sending monsters hurling through the air.

In this regard, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a ton of fun to play and unlock each monster, with learning each monster’s moveset to use in local or online multiplayer being particularly fun.

1990s Godzilla, Anguirus, Megalon, and Gigan are all available to play as from the get-go

However, aside from unlocking every monster and playing through Adventure Mode with each monster, there’s not much incentive to keep on playing the game for long. Sure, players can unlock G-Force sighting video clips, monster photos but there’s no system to customize the monsters and most maps play far too similar to each other.

I can barely tell the difference between most cities aside from a few notable landmarks like Seattle’s space needle. That's okay though as the remaster is clearly not trying to reinvent the wheel or even include features from DAMM’s sequels since this is a remaster first and foremost, not a proper reimagining or a true sequel.

While I didn’t play Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee growing up, I can immediately feel the sixth console generation charm of the game from its remasters right from the start. It’s a fighting game that people can instantly have a ton of fun playing through as they wreak havoc throughout some of the planet's most famous cities and fight against some of cinema’s most famous monsters in single-player or comedic local or online matches.

With how uncommon it is to find brand-new local co-op games these days, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered feels like a breath of fresh air and it’s a game that young Godzilla fans will certainly want to pick up before the year’s end. Plus, with how affordable the remaster is both in terms of its price and its remarkably small file size, DAMMR is a game that any fan of Godzilla or fun couch co-op games in general should pick up soon as it will likely make for fantastic holiday gift. DAMMR might not have all that of an engaging story or even a ton of side features but it more than makes up for those flaws by being a simple fun game to create kaiju chaos solo or with friends.

If you enjoy beating people up but not for a long time, check out these fighting games you can finish in under 10 hours.

#4509. Tesla Sold FSD To Koreans Who Still Can't Use It. Now It's Facing A Complaint

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla's Full Self-Driving will turn 10 years old next month. Nearly four of those years have labeled FSD as an official beta product, and over two additional years have been under the new "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" rebranding. Whatever the name, the car that is in your driveway today still can't technically drive itself without you being responsible for what happens behind the wheel.

Needless to say, some drivers are getting impatient—especially those who have purchased FSD for multiple cars, or have managed to pay off their car loan before getting unsupervised FSD. Now a consumer advocacy group in South Korea is firing back to demand answers and accountability.

The rollout of FSD in Korea is even more confusing that it is in the U.S. thanks to another layer of complexity: where the vehicle was manufactured.

According to Reuters, only about 20% of the Teslas registered in South Korea—vehicles assembled in the United States—are actually eligible to enable the Full Self-Driving software. That's because those vehicles meet the U.S. Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, and a trade agreement with the U.S. designates those standards as acceptable to enter Korea without additional modification.

The majority of the remaining vehicles have been manufactured in China, where no agreement (or supplementary safety certification) for its FSD software exists today. Since 2023, Tesla has imported about 170,000 of these Shanghai-built cars with the volume of Chinese-built cars increasing five-fold last year alone. In fact, 99% of Teslas imported into China in 2025 were from China and ineligible to activate FSD.

A complaint being filed by Korean consumer advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty (reviewed by Reuters) with the Korean Fair Trade Commission alleges that Tesla has still been collecting money from buyers for its FSD software for over three years, despite the software not being available to buyers due to this restriction. This meant buyers forked over as much as $6,800 for the feature, but haven't actually been able to switch it on. Some buyers instead resorted to enabling region-locked FSD via a "jailbreak," which is seen as a safety circumvention and led to owners facing jail time or fines of up to $15,000.

Things get a bit more complicated given the recent legal loss raised by dozens of Tesla owners who had their lawsuit thrown out of Korean courts just last week. According to the ruling from the Seoul Central District Court, Tesla didn't technically break its contractual obligations with the 88 owners who requested full refunds via a lawsuit filed in 2024.

The court acknowledged that Tesla's delivery of the features promised with FSD hinged on certain technical advances and regulatory approval that buyers were aware could "take considerable time to become available," according to reporting by the South China Morning Post. If those didn't happen, the court says that Tesla isn't in the wrong.

The complaint by Citizens United raises additional questions about the way that Tesla advertises its vehicles to consumers. And they're not the first. The KFTC confirmed to Reuters that it launched a probe into Tesla's advertising earlier this year, but declined to comment further. Tesla didn't respond to the outlet's request for comment.

Whether or not this avenue will result in action after the court's ruling that buyers weren't entitled to a refund is unclear.

#4508. Peterbilt makes it easier than ever for government fleets to go electric

Legendary truck brand Peterbilt is lowering procurement barriers for state and municipal fleets looking to electrify their assets by adding its growing lineup of medium- and heavy-duty battery electric trucks to its cooperative purchasing Agreement with Sourcewell.

The expanded purchasing contract, extended through July 2028, provides Sourcewell’s more than 50,000 member organizations access to competitively solicited contracts with pre-negotiated pricing and terms across the Peterbilt brand’s full lineup of Class 5-8 commercial trucks. That contract allows eligible agencies to streamline procurement by sourcing Peterbilt’s on-highway, vocational and medium-duty BEVs through Sourcewell’s pre-negotiated agreement, potentially eliminating the need to go through a long, agonizing bidding process of their own.

“Our long-standing relationship with Sourcewell reflects Peterbilt’s commitment to delivering solutions tailored to the unique needs of public fleets,” explains Erik Johnson, assistant general manager of sales and marketing at Peterbilt. “By adding our electric vehicles to the contract and eliminating lengthy bidding processes, we’re helping organizations maximize uptime and invest their resources where it matters most, keeping their communities running.”

I hear some of you asking, “Why is this important, and what exactly is Sourcewell?” And you’re very smart to ask.

See, when your state or local government decides it needs a new truck, it can’t just call up someone’s cousin and cut an inflated check backed by your tax dollars (regardless of what you saw on Fox News). Instead, public agencies generally have to follow competitive purchasing rules that are designed to ensure fairness, transparency, and responsible use of taxpayer money. That can mean writing and publishing a request for proposals (RFP), publicly soliciting bids, evaluating competing offers, and even allowing public comments that can all-too easily devolve into 17 hours of Pawnee-level discourse among stakeholders (real and imagined) about the relative merits of competing proposals.

Sourcewell is a government agency that basically does all that ahead of time, publishing RFPs, soliciting ,and evaluating bids against established criteria, then awarding contracts through a transparent, auditable process that makes competitively negotiated pricing available to more than 50,000 government, education and nonprofit organizations across the US and Canada.

In practice, that means your local government fleets can leverage Sourcewell to quickly adapt to pressing needs in a way that doesn’t bypass the bidding process (which would be illegal), but which effectively says, “we trust Sourcewell’s process.”

You can check out the full text of Sourcewell’s contract with Peterbilt, below, then let us know what you think of Pete’s efforts to electrify your local government fleet in the comments.

#4507. The 2027 Chevy Silverado EV Gets A Power Bump And A NACS Port

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Chevrolet is giving its most expensive electric pickup a power bump for the 2027 model, not that it needed it. The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss with the Max Range battery pack now puts down a whopping 750 horsepower and 775 pound-feet of torque, as reported by GM Authority.

That’s 25 hp more than the outgoing model, but it’s worth noting that the maximum output is only available when activating the Wide Open Watts (WOW) mode, which pushes every metric to the top for maximum acceleration, but isn’t intended for regular use. Chevrolet doesn’t say how much power the Silverado EV makes when the WOW mode is disabled.

The power figures of all other Silverado EV trims stay the same, but as with all 2027 General Motors EVs, they now come from the factory with a native Tesla-style NACS charging port. This enables them to pull up to Tesla Superchargers and other NACS-equipped chargers and top up without needing an adapter.

For 2027, the electric pickup also gains a few new cameras. The Cabin Glance feature shows a live video feed of the car’s interior on the infotainment screen. Then, there’s Security Recording, which records video from the vehicle’s on-board cameras when the alarm is triggered. Last but not least, the Surround Vision Recorder acts as an on-board video security system that continuously records footage while the car is in use, much like Tesla’s Dashcam feature.

The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado EV is slightly more expensive than the outgoing model on all trims. The base Silverado EV Standard Range starts at $56,085 (including destination charges), $700 more than the previous model. Meanwhile, the LT and Trail Boss trims with the Extended Range battery are now $1,000 more than last year, while the top-spec Trail Boss with the Max Range battery now starts at $90,395, or $1,200 more than the 2026 model.

All Silverado EV trims come with a dual-motor, all-wheel-drive setup. The entry-level WT trim has 510 hp and 490 or 580 lb-ft of torque, depending on the battery capacity. The LT Standard Range gets 605 hp and 605 lb-ft of torque, followed by the LT Extended Range, with 645 hp and 765 lb-ft of torque. The Trail Boss Extended Range has 625 hp and 775 lb-ft of torque, and the Trail Boss Max Range pushes the power figure up to 750 hp.

Besides more power and torque, the Trail Boss also comes with a two-inch suspension lift, a more aggressive off-road body kit, 35-inch tires, four-wheel steering as standard, and some new driving modes. Despite the trail-oriented kit, the Trail Boss is the longest-range model in the lineup, with up to 478 miles on the Max Range battery.

The RST trim, which used to be the top option, has been discontinued. Production of the 2027 Chevy Silverado EV kicked off at GM’s Factory Zero in Michigan last month.

#4506. Our Long-Term 2026 Honda Passport Is Still a Hot Commodity

With its plush interior and a commodious cargo hold, our boxy Honda has become the car-board-lottery jackpot for those planning a road trip.

“I’ve finally won!” exclaims technical editor Austin Irwin in response to snagging our long-term 2026 Honda Passport TrailSport for the weekend. Typically, it’s sports cars, rolling palaces, or vehicles with a manual transmission that elicit that type of reaction during our weekly sign-out process, not mid-size two-row SUVs. But the Passport really does have that effect on folks around here.

While it’s nowhere near the most engaging vehicle at our office at any given time, our sunburnt Honda’s allure comes from its ability to effortlessly eat both cargo and miles in large sums. Depending on your weekend plans, that can be far more valuable than the Hattori Hanzō–sharp steering precision of a 911 or the rewarding snick of a Miata’s six-speed shifter.

In the 10,000 miles since we last checked in, a handful of editors have taken full advantage of the Passport’s strengths. In just a few short months, it checked Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Ohio off its regional-visitation checklist, with one sentiment echoed by the three staffers upon returning from their respective excursions: The Passport is a damn good road tripper.

See all results for new 2026 Honda Passport for sale near 20147

“Taking the Passport on a trip through Ohio to Hocking Hills was very enjoyable,” said online production assistant Sarah Taylor, who specifically called out its smooth ride and competent handling on winding mountain roads. Senior social media editor Carter Fry also joined in on praising the Honda’s on-road demeanor, noting that the SUV “is so well balanced considering its size and all-terrain tires.” A plush ride and confidence-inspiring handling are important traits on long-distance trips, but the Passport’s comfortable and expansive interior is what really cements it as our resident road-trip hero.

“Cavernous,” “spacious,” and “generous” have all appeared in the Passport’s in-car logbook to describe its cargo accommodations, and it is indeed very roomy back there by mid-size-SUV standards. In our testing, we managed to stuff under its liftgate 16 carry-on suitcases with the rearmost seats in their upright position and 38 carry-ons with the rear bench folded down. That’s 13 and nine more than will fit in a Toyota 4Runner, respectively. Managing news editor Eric Stafford did his best to stretch the Passport’s people and stuff-hauling capabilities to their limit on a ski trip to northern Wisconsin and reported that there was more than enough room to comfortably accommodate three guys and all their gear. So far, no one has been able to find anything that doesn’t fit in the Passport's cargo hold, but we’ll keep brainstorming.

As far as grievances are concerned, there haven’t been many. Several editors have reported software issues related to phone pairing, Google Maps connectivity, and Apple CarPlay glitches. On one occasion, the infotainment screen went blank but continued to play music from the grave. On another, the GPS display within the digital gauge cluster got confused and gave up despite that Android Auto was running with no connectivity issues. Both of those incidents were resolved with a simple restart. Aside from that, there’s an ambiguous logbook comment likening the Passport’s interior to “something you’d order out of an L.L. Bean catalog,” but it's unclear whether that was meant as a compliment or a dig. Depends on how much you like cable-knit sweaters, we suppose.

See all results for new 2026 Honda Passport for sale near 20147

There isn’t much to report from a service or repair standpoint, either. Since we took in the Passport for its 10,000-mile oil service, which was covered under Honda’s one-year, 12,000-mile complimentary maintenance coverage, the sole out-of-pocket expense we’ve incurred was for the Passport’s 20,000-mile service, which included an oil and filter change, a tire rotation, and an inspection, for a total of $184. The only change to the TrailSport’s hardware was a swap back to its original 275/60R-18 General Grabber A/T Sport tires after the shedding of its Continental VikingContact 8 winters, but we handled that ourselves.

While it’s uncommon for a family SUV to be a first-round pick in an office full of performance-pilled enthusiasts, it’s clear why our long-term Passport is so highly coveted. With its coddling seats, plush but poised ride quality, and seemingly boundless cargo hold, the Passport is a hard act to beat when you’re staring down a thousand-mile road trip. As long as C/D staffers remain adventurous, we’re sure that the Passport’s key fob will continue to be fought over in the 20,000 miles to come.
